headline: Preprint reports that prompt-specific scorer error can alter LLM evaluation contrasts
summary: An arXiv workshop preprint studies whether an automatic scorer can distort comparisons between prompt conditions even when its pooled accuracy looks high. In an exploratory UUP-Bench case study, a +0.093 Certainty-only-minus-Neutral contrast from automatic scoring became +0.023 under both the primary and secondary LLM raters; the primary-rater interval [-0.059,+0.053] included zero. The authors also report pooled F1 of 0.916 in a separate 288-response audit while arm-level false-positive rates ranged from 0.026 to 0.333. The paper argues that evaluations should audit each arm and test the target contrast on matched cases. All labels came from LLM raters rather than human ground truth; the study is limited to one constructed benchmark and has not been independently reproduced.
